en: To Hölderlin (August 1796)
zh: 致荷尔德林（1796年8月）

en: Around me and in me dwells calm — the never-weary care of busy men sleeps, they give me freedom and leisure — thanks to you, you my liberatrix, o night!

With a white veil of mist the moon draws around the uncertain boundaries of the distant hills; friendly the bright stripe of the lake blinks over to me, the day's tedious clamor removes memory, as if years lay between it and now.

Your image, beloved, steps before me, and the joy of the days that fled; but soon it yields to the sweeter hopes of seeing you again — already the scene of the long-yearned-for, fiery embrace paints itself for me; then the scene of questions, of the more secret mutual spying out, what in bearing, expression, way of mind has changed in the friend since that time — the bliss of certainty, to find the loyalty of the old covenant firmer, riper still, the covenant that no oath sealed, to live only for free truth, never, never to enter into peace with the statute that regulates opinion and feeling.

Now the wish negotiates with the more sluggish actuality, the wish that lightly carried me over mountains and rivers to you — but soon a sigh proclaims their quarrel, and with it the dream of sweet imaginings flees away.
zh: 我周围、我心中住着安宁，——忙碌的人们那从不疲倦的操心睡着了，他们给我自由和闲暇——谢谢你，我的解放者，啊，夜！
月亮用白色的雾纱围住远山那不确定的边界；湖面明亮的一条友好地朝我这边闪烁，白天那令人腻烦的喧闹把记忆推开，仿佛它和现在之间隔着好些年。
你的形象，心爱的人，走到我面前，还有那些逃走的日子的快乐；但它很快就让位给重逢那更甜的盼望——那期盼已久、火热的拥抱的场面已经在我眼前展开；接着是问话的场面，是更隐秘的彼此打量的场面：朋友在这些日子里，姿态、表情、心性上有什么变了，——然后是那份确信的欢喜：发现旧日盟约的忠诚更牢固、更成熟了，那个没有誓言封印的盟约，只为自由的真理而活，绝不、绝不与那条规定意见和感受的成规讲和。
现在，愿望跟更迟钝的现实性商谈起来，这愿望曾轻易地把我越过山岭、河流带到你身边——可一声叹息很快宣告了它们的争执，随着它，甜美想象力的梦也逃走了。

en: My eye rises up to the vault of the eternal heaven, to you, o shining star of the night!

And the forgetting of all wishes, all hopes streams down out of your eternity; (the sense loses itself in the gazing, what I called mine vanishes, I give myself over to the immeasurable, I am in it, am everything, am only it.
To the returning thought it is alien, it dreads the infinite, and in astonishment it does not grasp the depth of this gazing.
To the sense imagination brings the eternal near, weds it to shape)67) — welcome, you sublime spirits, lofty shadows, from whose brow completion shines!
It does not frighten him — I feel it is also my homeland's ether, the seriousness, the splendor that flows around you.
Ha! if the gates of your sanctuary would now spring open of themselves, o Ceres, you who throned in Eleusis!

Drunk with inspiration I would now feel the shudders of your nearness, would understand your revelations, I would interpret the high sense of the images, would hear the hymns at the gods' meals, the lofty sayings of their council. —
zh: 我的眼睛升向永恒天空的穹顶，升向你，啊，夜的光辉星辰！
而一切愿望、一切希望的遗忘，从你的永恒里流下来；（感觉在凝视中消失，我曾称作我的东西消逝了，我把自己交给那不可度量者，我在它里面，我是一切，我只是它。
对返回来的思想来说它变得陌生，思想对无限感到害怕，惊讶着，领会不了这凝视的深度。
想象力把永恒拉近感觉，让它与形象联姻)67)——欢迎你们，崇高的精神，高高的影子，圆满从你们的额头放光！
他并不惊惶，——我感觉到，环绕你们的那份严肃、那份光辉，也是我故乡的以太。
哈！但愿你的圣所之门此刻自行敞开，啊，刻瑞斯，你曾在厄琉西斯端坐！
此刻我会醉在灵感里，感到你临近时的战栗，懂得你的启示，我会解出那些形象的高意，会听见众神用餐时的颂歌，听见他们议事时的高论。——

en: But your halls have fallen silent, o goddess!

Fled back into Olympus from the hallowed altars is the circle of the gods, fled from the desecrated grave of mankind is the genius of innocence, that conjured them here! — The wisdom of your priests is silent; no tone of the holy consecration
zh: 可你的殿堂已经沉寂，啊，女神！
众神的圈子已经逃回奥林匹斯，从那些神圣化的祭坛上逃走；纯真的守护神也从被亵渎的人类坟墓旁逃走，正是它把众神招引到这里！——你祭司的智慧沉默无声；没有一声神圣的祝圣

en: has saved itself to us — and in vain the researcher's curiosity seeks more than love of wisdom (the seekers possess it and despise you) — in order to master it they dig for words into which your high sense might have been stamped!
In vain!
Perhaps they only snatched dust and ashes, into which your life never ever returns to them.
But amid mould and the soulless the eternally dead also took their pleasure! — the easily contented — in vain — no sign of your festivals remained, no trace of any image.
To the son of consecration the fullness of the high teachings, the depth of the inexpressible feeling was far too holy for him to deem dry signs worthy of them.
Thought itself does not grasp the soul, which, sunk outside time and space in foreboding of infinity, forgets itself and now awakens again to consciousness.
Whoever wanted to speak of it to others, even if he spoke with tongues of angels, would feel the poverty of words.
He dreads to have thought the holy so small, to have made it so small through them, that speech seems to him a sin
zh: 已经逃到我们这里——而研究者那比爱智慧更多的好奇，白白地寻找（搜寻者占有着它，却鄙视你）——为了掌握它，他们挖找字词，想把你那高意印进去！
白费！
他们也许只抓到了尘土和灰烬，对他们来说，你的生命永远不会再回到其中。
可在霉烂和没有灵魂的东西中间，那些永远死掉的也自得其乐！——那些容易满足的人——白费——你的节庆没有留下任何标志，任何图像都没有留下痕迹。
对祝圣之子来说，那些高深学说的丰富、那不可言说的感受的深度，都太神圣了，他不认为干巴巴的符号配得上它们。
思想本身就把握不了那灵魂：它在时间和空间之外，沉入对无限的预感，忘掉自己，如今又重新醒到意识中来。
谁要想把它对别人讲，哪怕用天使的舌头讲，也会感到言辞的贫乏。
他害怕自己把神圣想得这么小，通过言辞把它弄得这么小，以致说话在他看成了罪

en: And that he, living, shuts his mouth.

What the consecrated one thus forbade himself, a wise law forbade to the poorer spirits, not to make known what he had seen, heard, felt in the holy night: so that not even to the better ones the noise of their mischief should disturb him in his devotion, their hollow word-junk should not make him angry at the holy itself, this should not be so trampled into the mud that one even entrusted it to memory — that it should not become the toy and the ware of the sophist, which he sold by the obol, the cloak of the eloquent hypocrite, or even the rod of the happy boy, and so empty in the end that it had the root of its life only in the echo of foreign tongues.
Your sons, goddess, carried your honor stingily, not in the street and market, they kept it in the inner sanctuary of the breast.
Therefore you did not live on their mouth.
Their life honored you.
In their deeds you still live.
This night too I heard you, holy divinity, you; often the life of your children also reveals you to me, often I sense you as the soul of their deeds!
You are the high sense, the faithful faith, which, a divinity, even if everything perishes, does not waver.
zh: 于是他活着，把自己的嘴闭上。

祝圣者这样自己对自己禁止的事，一条明智的法律也向那些更贫弱的精神禁止了：不许说出他在神圣之夜看见、听见、感受到的东西，——免得那些较好的人也以他们胡闹的喧嚷打扰他的虔敬，他们空空洞洞的词句杂碎惹他对神圣本身发怒，免得这东西被这样踩进泥里，甚至被人托付给记忆，——免得它变成智者的玩具和货物，他按奥波尔一份份地卖掉，变成能言善辩的伪善者的外套，甚至变成快活孩子的教鞭，最后变得那么空，以致它生命的根只长在别人舌头的回声里。
你的儿子们，女神，吝啬地守着你的荣誉，不拿到街巷和市场上去，他们把它保存在胸中那内在的圣所里。
因此你并不活在他们嘴上。
他们的生活尊敬你。
在他们的行为里你还活着。
这个夜晚我也听见了你，神圣的神性，听见了你；你的孩子们的生活也常常向我启示你，我常常预感到你，把你当作他们行为的灵魂！
你就是那高意，那忠诚的信仰，它本身是神性，即使一切都沉沦，也不动摇。

7.zh: [《德国观念论最古老的体系纲领》]68)

en: — an ethics.

Since the whole of metaphysics will in the future fall into morals — of which Kant with his two practical postulates has given only an example and has exhausted nothing — this ethics will be nothing other than a complete system of all ideas, or, what is the same, of all practical postulates.
The first idea is naturally the representation of myself as an absolutely free being.

With the free, self-conscious being there emerges at the same time a whole world — out of nothing — the only true and thinkable creation out of nothing. — Here I will descend into the fields of physics; the question is this: How must a world be constituted for a moral being?
I would like once again to give wings to our slow physics, which trudges laboriously through experiments.
zh: ——一种伦理学。
因为今后整个形而上学都归入道德——对此康德用他的两个实践公设只给出了一个例子，什么也没有穷尽——，所以这种伦理学不是别的，而是一个关于一切观念、或者说得一样，关于一切实践公设的完整体系。
第一个观念自然就是关于我自己作为一个绝对自由的存在者的表象。
随着自由的、有自我意识的存在者，同时出现的是一整个的世界——从无中出来——这是唯一真实而可设想的从无中创造。——这里我要下到物理学的田野上去；问题就是这个：一个世界对于一个道德的存在者来说必须是怎么样的？
我想给我们那缓慢的、在实验上艰难迈步的物理学再一次插上翅膀。

en: Thus, if philosophy supplies the ideas and experience the data, we can finally get the physics on a grand scale that I expect from later ages.
It does not seem that present-day physics could satisfy a creative spirit such as ours is or ought to be.
zh: 这样，如果哲学提供观念、经验提供数据，我们最终就能得到那种大格局的物理学，那是我从后来的时代所期待的。
现在的物理学似乎不能使一个创造性的精神感到满足，像我们这样的精神、或者应当成为这样的精神。

en: From nature I come to the work of man.
With the idea of humanity in the lead, I want to show that there is no idea of the state, because the state is something mechanical, just as there is no idea of a machine.
Only what is an object of freedom is called an idea.
So we must go beyond the state! — For every state must treat free men as a mechanical cogwork; and it should not do that; so it should cease.
You see for yourselves that here all the ideas of eternal peace and so on are only subordinate ideas of a higher idea.
At the same time I want to set down here the principles for a history of humanity and to strip the whole wretched work of man — state, constitution, government, legislation — down to the skin.

Finally come the ideas of a moral world, of the deity, of immortality — the overthrow of all false faith, the persecution of the priesthood, which lately feigns reason, by reason itself. — Absolute freedom of all spirits that bear the intellectual world within themselves and may seek neither God nor immortality outside themselves.
zh: 从自然，我转到人的作品上。
以人类的观念打头，我要指出，没有关于国家的观念，因为国家是某种机械的东西，正如没有关于机器的观念一样。
只有是自由的对象的东西，才叫观念。
所以我们必须超出国家！——因为每个国家都必定把自由的人当作机械的齿轮装置来对待；而它不该这样做；所以它应当停止。
你们自己就看得出，这里所有关于永久和平等等的观念，都只是一个更高观念的下属观念。
同时我要在这里放下为一部人类史准备的原则，并且把国家、宪法、政府、立法这整套可怜的人的作品剥到见皮。
最后来的是一个道德世界、神性、不朽这些观念，——推翻一切伪信仰，用理性本身去追究那种近来假冒理性的教士阶层。——一切精神的绝对自由，这些精神在自己心里带着理智世界，而不可以到自己之外去寻找上帝和不朽。

en: Finally the idea that unites all, the idea of beauty, the word taken in a higher Platonic sense.
I am now convinced that the highest act of reason, the one in which it embraces all ideas, is an aesthetic act, and that truth and goodness are sistered only in beauty.
The philosopher must possess as much aesthetic power as the poet.
The people without aesthetic sense are our letter-philosophers.
The philosophy of spirit is an aesthetic philosophy.
One cannot be ingenious in anything, one cannot reason ingeniously even about history — without aesthetic sense.
Here it shall become evident what those who understand no ideas actually lack — and they confess honestly enough that everything is dark to them as soon as it goes beyond tables and registers.
zh: 最后是把一切都结合起来的那个观念，美的观念，这词要在更高的柏拉图意义上理解。
我现在确信，理性的最高行动，即它把一切观念都包含在内的那个行动，是一个审美行动，而且真与善只有在美之中才结为姐妹。
哲学家必须和诗人一样具有同样多的审美力量。
没有审美感的人就是我们的字母哲学家。
精神的哲学是一门审美的哲学。
人在任何事情上都不可能机智，甚至对历史也不可能机智地议论——没有审美感的话。
这里应当明白显出，那些不懂观念的人究竟缺的是什么——他们够老实地承认，一超出表格和登记簿，一切对他们都是昏黑的。

en: Poetry thereby receives a higher dignity, it becomes in the end again what it was in the beginning — the teacher of humanity; for there is no philosophy, no history any more, poetry alone will outlive all the remaining sciences and arts.
zh: 诗由此获得更高的尊严，它最终又成为它起初所是的东西——人类的教师；因为不再有哲学、不再有历史，唯有诗艺会比其余一切科学和艺术活得都长。

en: At the same time we so often hear that the great crowd must have a sensuous religion.
Not only the great crowd, the philosopher too needs it.
Monotheism of reason and of the heart, polytheism of the imagination and of art, this is what we need.
zh: 同时我们又常常听到，大群的人必须有一种感性的宗教。
不只是大群的人，哲学家也需要它。
理性与心的一神教，想象力和艺术的多神教，这才是我们所需要的。

en: First I will speak here of an idea which, as far as I know, has never yet entered any man's mind - we must have a new mythology, but this mythology must stand in the service of the ideas, it must become a mythology of reason.
zh: 首先我要在这里谈一个观念，据我所知，它还从来没有进过任何一个人的头脑——我们必须有一种新的神话，但这种神话必须为诸观念服务，它必须成为一种理性的神话。

en: Before we make the ideas aesthetic, that is, mythological, they have no interest for the people; and conversely, before the mythology is rational, the philosopher must be ashamed of it.

Thus the enlightened and the unenlightened must at last reach out their hands to one another, the mythology must become philosophical and the people rational, and the philosophy must become mythological in order to make the philosophers sensuous.
Then eternal unity will reign among us.
Never again the contemptuous glance, never again the blind trembling of the people before its wise men and priests.
Only then does there await us an equal cultivation of all powers, of the individual as well as of all individuals.
No power will any longer be suppressed.
Then universal freedom and equality of spirits will reign! - A higher spirit, sent from heaven, must found this new religion among us, it will be the last, greatest work of mankind.
zh: 在我们把诸观念弄得审美，也就是弄得神话之前，它们引不起民众的兴趣；反过来，在神话成为理性的之前，哲学家必然为它感到羞愧。
这样，开明的人和不开明的人最终必须互相伸出手来，神话必须成为哲学的，民众必须变得理性，而哲学必须成为神话的，好让哲学家变得感性。
那时我们中间将盛行永恒的统一。
再也不会有那种轻蔑的目光，再也不会有民众在自己的智者和祭司面前那种盲目的颤抖。
到那时，才等着我们的是所有力量的同等培养，无论对单个的人，还是对所有的个体。
再也不会有任何力量遭到压制。
那时将盛行精神的普遍自由和平等！——一个更高的精神，由天派来，必须在我们中间创立这种新的宗教，它将是人类最后一件、最大的作品。

en: 69) A faith is called positive in which the practical is present theoretically - the originally subjective only as an objective; a religion that sets up representations of something objective that cannot become subjective as the principle of life and of the actions.

Practical activity acts freely, without union of an opposite, without being determined by this - it does not bring unity into a given manifold, but is unity70) itself, which only saves itself against the manifold opposite, which with respect to the practical capacity always remains unconnected; the practical unity is asserted in that the opposite is entirely sublated.
zh: 69) 一种信仰被称为实证的，在它里面，实践的东西以理论的方式现成存在——原本主观的东西只作为一个客观的东西；这是一种宗教，它把关于某种不能成为主观的客观东西的表象，立为生命和行动的原则。
实践的活动自由地行动，不与一个对立的东西结合，也不被这个对立的东西规定——它并不把统一带进一种被给予的杂多，而本身就是那个统一70)，它只是针对杂多的对立东西来拯救自己，而那杂多的对立东西就实践能力而言永远是没有结合的；实践的统一是这样得到主张的：对立的东西被完全扬弃。

en: All moral commandments are demands to assert this unity against drives; the former differ only in that they are directed against different drives - this unity represented.
zh: 一切道德的诫命都是主张这种统一以对抗冲动的要求；它们彼此的不同只在于它们针对的是不同的冲动——这种统一被表象出来。

en: What is: concept of morality?
The moral concepts do not have objects in the sense in which the theoretical concepts have objects.

The object of the former is always the I; the object of the latter the not-I. - The object of the moral concept is a certain determination of the I, which, in order to become a concept, in order to be cognized, in order to be able to become object, is opposed to the I as otherwise determined, is regarded as an accident of the I, is excluded from the determination of the I that now cognizes. - Concept is a reflected activity.

A moral concept that has not arisen in this way, a concept without the activity, is a positive concept; yet it is at the same time supposed to become practical; it is only something cognized, a given, something objective, and receives its power, its force, its effectiveness only through an object arousing respect or fear, before which we perish, to which we would have to succumb, if in those concepts the way to that object, to the hope of being spared, were not opened up for us, whereby agreement would become possible.
zh: 什么是：道德的概念？
道德的概念并不是在理论的概念拥有对象的那种意义上拥有对象。
前者的对象永远是自我，后者的对象是非我。——道德概念的对象是自我的某种规定，这种规定为了成为一个概念，为了被认识，为了能够成为对象，就与那个以另外方式被规定的自我相对立，就被看作自我的一个偶性，就被从此刻正在认识的那个自我的规定中排除出去。——概念是一种被反思的活动。
一个不是以这种方式产生的道德概念，一个没有这种活动的概念，是一个实证的概念；但它同时应当成为实践的；它只是一件被认识到的东西，一个被给予的东西，某种客观的东西，并且只有通过一个唤起敬重或恐惧的对象才获得它的权力、它的力量、它的效力——在这个对象面前我们会消亡，我们会不得不屈服于它，如果不是在那些概念里为我们打开了通向那个对象、通向被宽免的希望的道路，从而一致才成为可能的话。

en: The positive moral concept is capable of losing the character of positivity when the activity that it expresses is itself developed and acquires force, - but what one ordinarily calls positive is of such a nature that it is not a reflected activity of ourselves but something objective, and can never lay aside this character.
zh: 实证的道德概念能够失去实证性的特征，如果它表达的活动自身得到发展并取得力量的话，——但人们通常称为实证的那种东西，其性质是：它不是我们自身的一种被反思的活动，而是某种客观的东西，并且永远不能卸下这个特征。

en: The moral can indeed also become objective, in that it is represented and conceived, but the consciousness is always connected with it, or can immediately be produced, that we ourselves, our own free force and activity, is the object of cognition.
The moral and the objective in the ordinary sense are directly opposed to each other.
zh: 道德的东西固然也能变成客观的，因为它被表象、被把握；但总有这样一种意识与它相连，或者这种意识马上就能造出来：我们自己，我们自己自由的力量和活动，是认识的对象。
道德的东西和通常意义上的客观的东西，恰恰彼此对立。

en: The infinite object, its way of acting, are also positive for the capacity of cognition; miracles, revelations, appearances.
zh: 无限的对象，以及它的行动方式，对认识能力来说也是实证的；奇迹、启示、现象。

en: In intuition no whole is to be given, the capacity of cognition is to give up the laws of its essence, to imagine a whole into a part, to know a suffering, and not the same quantity of activity is to be given to it in the appearance, and intuition is never to think this as such a whole.
The activity, the cause, is to be something unknown, the one member of the change no object, no not-I and also no I, not as with the effects of human beings, where one member is an I.
zh: 在直观里不应有任何整体被给予，认识能力应当放弃它本质的规律，即对一个部分想象出一个整体，应当认识一种受动；而且在现象里不应有同等分量的活动被给予它，直观也永远不应把它想成这样一个整体。
活动、原因应当是某种未知的东西，变化的那一项不是对象，不是非我，也不是自我——不像在人的作用那里，那里有一项是自我。

en: The essence of the practical I consists in the going-beyond of ideal activity over the real and in the demand that objective activity should be equal to the infinite.

Practical faith is faith in that ideal; now faith is positive when that going-beyond as well as the demand of equality is given - this demand can become given only through a mighty and dominating objective (authority), which, and whose way of acting, however, cannot be conceived by us; in that we conceived it, it would be determined by us - its modes of operation must be miracles for us, which are impossible for us, i.e. they presuppose an activity that we do not recognize as the activity of an I, and thereby they differ from the actions that we recognize as actions of free beings, in that they are actions of an I.
zh: 实践自我的本质在于理想的活动对现实的东西的超出，以及在于这个要求：客观的活动应当等于无限的活动。

实践的信仰就是对那个理想的信仰；现在，如果那种超出以及相等的要求被给予了，信仰就是实证的——这个要求只能通过一个强大而支配性的客观之物（权威）被给予，但它以及它的行动方式，我们却无法把握；一旦我们把握了它，它就会被我们规定——它的各种作用方式对我们来说必须是奇迹，是对于我们不可能的奇迹，也就是说，它们预设了一种活动，我们不把这种活动认作一个自我的活动；而它们由此区别于我们认作自由存在者的行动的那些行动，即：它们是一个自我的行动。

en: In the case of the moral end that we attribute to the providence of the deity, we do not reflect on its remaining essence, which is unknown to us, but here we judge that its activity is to that extent the activity of an I.
zh: 在我们加给神性护佑的那个道德目的上，我们并不反思它其余那些我们不认识的本质，而是在这里下判断说，它的活动就此而言是一个自我的活动。

en: The other extreme from depending on an object is that of fearing the objects, the flight from them, the fear of union, the highest subjectivity.
zh: 依赖于一个对象的另一个极端，就是害怕这些对象，逃避它们，害怕结合，是最高的主体性。

en: Objective
zh: 客观的

en: 1. the actual in space,
zh: 1. 空间中的现实之物，

en: 2. inner determinations objectively, with the consciousness that they are inner determinations,
zh: 2. 内在规定客观地存在，并带有它们是内在规定的意识，

en: 3. inner determinations without the consciousness that they are inner determinations.
zh: 3. 内在规定，却没有它们是内在规定的意识。

en: Religion is the free veneration of the deity.
Merely subjective religion without imagination is uprightness.
zh: 宗教是对神性的自由崇拜。
没有想象力的、单纯主观的宗教，就是正直。

en: To comprehend is to dominate.
To animate the objects is to make them gods.
zh: 理解就是支配。
让对象活起来，就是把它们变成神。

en: To consider a stream as it must fall by the laws of gravity into the lower regions and is confined and pressed by the ground and the banks, means to comprehend it, to give it a soul, to take part in it as in one's equal, — means to make it a god.

But because a stream, a tree can at the same time also be an object, subjected to mere necessity, just as deified human beings too are distinguished from the state in which they were mere human beings, so they are mere demigods, not the eternal, necessary ones.

Where subject and object, or freedom and nature, are thought as united in such a way that nature is freedom, that subject and object are not to be separated, there is the divine — such an ideal is the object of every religion.
A deity is subject and object at once; one cannot say of it that it is subject in opposition to objects, or that it has objects.
zh: 看着一条溪流按重力的法则必须落向低处，被地面和两岸限制、挤压，这就算是以概念把握它，给它一个灵魂，把它当作同类而与它休戚相关，——这就算是把它变成神。
可是，因为一条溪流、一棵树同时也可以是一个对象，受单纯的必然性支配，正如被奉为神的人也跟他们还是普通人时的那种状态区别开来，所以它们只是半神，不是那些永恒的、必然的神。
哪里把主体和客体、或者说自由和自然想成这样结合起来的，以致自然就是自由，主体和客体不可分离，哪里就有神圣的东西——这样一个理想就是每一种宗教的对象。
一个神既是主体又是客体，人们不能说它是与客体对立的主体，也不能说它拥有客体。

en: The theoretical syntheses become wholly objective, wholly opposed to the subject.
Practical activity annihilates the object and is wholly subjective — only in love alone is one at one with the object; it does not dominate and is not dominated.

This love, made into a being by the imagination, is the deity; the separated human being then has reverence, respect for it, — the human being at one within himself [has] love; to the former his bad conscience, the consciousness of division, gives fear of it.
zh: 理论性的综合变得完全客观，与主体完全对立。
实践活动消灭对象，完全是主观的——只有在爱里面，人才与对象合而为一，它不支配，也不被支配。
这种爱，被想象力做成本质，就是神性；分离的人于是对它怀有敬畏、敬重，——在自己内里合一的人则怀有爱；前者的坏良心、那种分裂的意识，使他害怕它。

en: That union one can call the union of the subject and the object, of freedom and nature, of the actual and the possible.
If the subject keeps the form of the subject, the object the form of the object, nature still nature, then no union is hit upon.
The subject, the free being, is the overpowering one, and the object, nature, the dominated one.
zh: 那种结合，可以叫作主体与客体的结合、自由与自然的结合、现实之物与可能之物的结合。
如果主体保持着主体的形式，客体保持着客体的形式，自然还是自然，那就没有达成任何结合。
主体，这自由的存在者，是占上风的一方，而客体，自然，是被支配的一方。

en: In old times the gods walked among human beings; the more the separation increased, the distance, the more the gods too detached themselves from human beings, and in exchange they gained in sacrifices, incense and service, — were more feared, until the separation went so far that the union can happen only through violence.
Love can take place only toward the like, toward the mirror, toward the echo of our essence.
zh: 在古老的时代，诸神还在人们中间行走；分离越是大起来，距离越是拉远，诸神也就越是脱离人，作为补偿，他们得到的献祭、香火和侍奉反而更多，——也更多被人畏惧，直到分离发展到这种地步，结合只能靠暴力才发生。
爱只能对着相同者发生，对着镜子、对着我们自己本质的回声发生。

en: 71) ... just as they come to know several kinds that are not hostile to them, they take several gods into their pantheon.

Your God be also our God, i. e. let us no longer consider ourselves as separate ones, but as united ones. — A people that scorns all foreign gods must carry the hatred of the whole human race in its bosom.
zh: 71)……正如他们认识了若干对他们并无敌意的种类，他们就把若干神祇接纳进他们的万神殿。
你们的神也是我们的神，也就是说，让我们不再把自己看作特殊者，而看作结合者。——一个鄙视一切外来神祇的民族，胸中必定怀着整个人类的仇恨。

en: Where the separation between the drive and actuality is so great that real pain arises, he does indeed posit, as the ground of this suffering, an independent activity and animates it, but since union with the pain is impossible, in that it is a suffering, union with that cause of the suffering is likewise impossible, and he sets it over against himself as a hostile being; had he never enjoyed any favor from it, he would ascribe to it a hostile nature that does not change; if he has already had joy from it, has already loved it, he must think the hostile disposition only as passing, and if he is conscious of any guilt, he recognizes in his pain the punishing hand of the deity, with which he previously lived in friendship.

But if he is conscious of his purity and has enough strength to be able to endure this complete separation, then he stands mightily over against an unknown power in which there is nothing human, over against fate, without submitting himself or otherwise effecting a union with it, which with a more powerful being could only be a servitude.
zh: 当冲动和现实性之间的分离大到产生了实际的痛苦，他固然把这痛苦的原因设定为一种独立的活动，并让它活起来，可是既然与痛苦结合是不可能的，因为痛苦就是一种受苦，那么与那痛苦原因的结合也同样不可能，于是他把这原因当作一个敌对的存在者摆在自己对面；要是他从未得到过它的任何恩惠，他就会把一种不会改变的敌对本性归给它；要是他已经从它那里得到过快乐，已经爱过它，他就只能把这种敌对的意向想成暂时的，而如果他意识到自己有某种罪责，他就在自己的痛苦里认出神性那只惩罚的手，而他先前是与它友好相处的。
可是，如果他意识到自己的纯洁，又有足够的力量承受这种完全的分离，他就强有力地站在一种未知的力量、一种其中没有任何人性的力量，也就是命运面前，既不屈服，也不与它达成别的什么结合，因为与一个更强大的存在者结合，只可能是奴役。

en: If, there where in nature there is eternal separation, the incompatible is united, there is positivity.
This united thing, this ideal is therefore object, and there is something in it that is not subject.
zh: 如果在自然界里有永恒分离的那个地方，不可结合的东西被结合起来了，那里就有实证性。
所以这个被结合起来的东西、这个理想就是客体，而且它里面有一种东西，不是主体。

en: The ideal we cannot posit outside us, otherwise it would be an object, — nor in us alone, otherwise it would be no ideal.
zh: 理想，我们不能把它设定在我们之外，否则它就是一个客体，——也不能只设定在我们之内，否则它就不是理想。

en: Religion is one with love.
The beloved is not opposed to us, he is one with our essence; we see only ourselves in him, and yet then he is again not we — a miracle that we are not able to grasp.
zh: 宗教与爱是一回事。
所爱的人并不与我们对立，他和我们的本质是一体的；我们在他身上只看见我们自己，可他又终究不是我们——一个我们把握不了的奇迹。

en: “The initiate (Plato, Phaedrus [251 A]), who once enjoyed the full sight of eternal beauty, when he looks upon a godlike face that is a good copy of beauty or of some other incorporeal idea, is at first frightened, and one of the former shudders seizes him; afterwards he looks closer and reveres it as a god; and if he did not fear the reputation of madness, he would sacrifice to the beloved as to an image and a god.”
zh: “那入了秘仪的人（柏拉图，《斐德若》[251 A]），从前曾享受到对永恒之美的完整观照，当他看到一个像神一样的脸、而这脸是美或者别的什么无形观念的一个良好摹本时，他起初就大吃一惊，旧日战栗中的一种就抓住了他；随后他凑近去看，像敬一个神那样敬它；要是他不怕被人说成发疯，他就会像对一尊雕像、一个神那样向所爱的人献祭。”

en: 72) ... to which end everything else serves, [and] nothing stands in struggle with this [end], in equal right; — as, for example, Abraham posits himself and his family and afterwards his people — or [as] the whole of Christendom posits itself as final end.

But the further this whole is extended, the more things are brought into the equality of dependence — if the cosmopolitan comprehends the whole human race in its whole —, the less falls to a single one from the dominion over the objects and from the favour of the ruling being; each individual loses so much the more in his value, in his claims, his independence; for his value was the share in the dominion; without the pride of being the centre of things, the end of the collective whole is for him the highest, and he despises himself as so small a part as all individuals.
zh: 72)……其余一切都为之服务的那个目的，没有任何东西在与它斗争时享有同等的权利；——例如亚伯拉罕把自己、把自己的家庭以及后来把自己的民族——或者〔如〕整个基督教界把自己设定为终极目的。
但这个整体扩展得越广，被摆进依赖之平等中的东西越多——如果世界公民把整个人类在其整体中把握起来——，那么从对客体的统治和对那统治着的存在者的恩宠里落到单个人身上的就越少；每个个人就越是失去自己的价值、自己的要求、自己的独立性；因为他的价值曾经是统治中的一份；没有了做万物中心的那种骄傲，集体整体的目的对他来说就是至高者，而他把自己看成和所有个人一样小的一部分，于是鄙视自己。

en: Because this love, for the sake of the dead, is only surrounded with matter, [and] the matter is in itself indifferent to it, and its essence consists in this, that man in his innermost nature is something opposed, something independent, that everything is outer world for him, which is therefore as eternal as he himself, so indeed his objects change, but they never fail him; as certainly as he is, they are, and his divinity; hence his calm in loss and his certain comfort that the loss will be replaced for him, because it can be replaced for him.
Matter is in this way absolute for man; but of course, if he himself were no more, then there would also be nothing more for him, and why should he too have to be?

That he would like to be is very intelligible; for outside his collection of limitations, his consciousness, there lies not the eternal union completed in itself, only the barren nothing, but to think himself in this, of course, man cannot endure.

He is only as something opposed; the opposed is reciprocally condition and conditioned; he must think himself outside his consciousness, no determining thing without something determined and conversely; neither is unconditional; neither carries the root of its essence in itself, each is only relatively necessary; the one is for the other and therefore also for itself only through a foreign power; the other is allotted to it through that power's favour and grace; there is nowhere, except in something foreign, an independent being, by which foreign thing everything is given to man and to which he must owe himself and immortality, for which he begs with trembling and fear.
zh: 因为这种爱为了死者的缘故，只是被材料包围着，而材料本身对它来说是无所谓的，它的本质在于：人在自己最内在的本性中是一个对立的东西、一个独立的东西，一切对他都是外部世界，而外部世界也就和他自己一样永恒，所以他的对象固然在变换，但它们从不缺在他那里；他多么确定地存在，它们和他的神性也就多么确定地存在；因此他在丧失时的安宁，和他那确定的安慰，即丧失会给他补回来，因为它是能够给他补回来的。
质料以这种方式对人来说是绝对的；不过当然，如果他自己不再存在了，那么对他来说也就什么都不再存在了，可他又为什么非得存在呢？
他想要存在，这是很好理解的；因为在他的那一堆限制、他的意识之外，并没有在自身中完成了的、永恒的结合，只有干枯的虚无，不过要人在其中想自己，他当然是受不了的。

他只是作为对立的东西而存在；对立的东西彼此互为条件和有条件者；他必须把自己想成在自己意识之外，没有规定者就没有被规定者，反过来也一样；哪一个都不是无条件的；哪一个都不在自己身上带着自己本质的根，每一个都只是相对必然的；这一个只通过一种外来的力量才为那一个而存在，因而也为它自己而存在；那一个则是靠这力量的恩宠和恩典分给它的；到处都没有一种独立的存在，除非在一个外来的东西里；人所有的一切都是这个外来的东西送的，他的自己和永生都必须感谢它，而这两样他是战战兢兢地乞求的。

en: True union, proper love takes place only among living beings that are equal in power and therefore through and through living for one another, from no side dead against one another; it excludes all oppositions, it is not understanding, whose relations always leave the manifold as manifold and whose unity is itself oppositions; it is not reason, which opposes its determining to the determined absolutely; it is nothing limiting, nothing limited, nothing finite; it is a feeling, but not a single feeling; out of the single feeling, because it is only a partial life, not the whole life, life presses through dissolution toward dispersion in the manifoldness of feelings and in order to find itself in this whole of manifoldness; in love this whole is not contained as in the sum of many particular, separated ones; in it life itself finds itself, as a doubling of itself, and unity of the same; life has, starting from the undeveloped unity, run through the circle through formation to a completed unity; over against the undeveloped unity stood the possibility of separation and the world; in development reflection produced ever more opposed things, which were united in satisfied drive, until it set the whole of man himself over against him, until love sublates reflection in complete objectlessness, robs the opposed of every character of something foreign, and life finds itself without further lack.
In love the separated is still there, but no longer as separated, [but] as something one, and the living feels the living.
zh: 真正的结合、本来意义上的爱，只发生在活的东西之间——它们力量相等，因此完全是为彼此而活的，没有哪一边是彼此相对的死东西；爱排除一切对立，它不是知性，知性的种种关系总是把杂多留作杂多，而它自己的统一本身就是种种对立；它不是理性，理性把自己的规定绝对地对立于被规定者；它不是任何限制着的东西，不是任何被限制的东西，不是任何有限的东西；它是一种感受，但不是单个的感受；生命从单个的感受里——因为它只是部分生命，不是整个生命——通过消解挤向消散，散入感受的杂多之中，为的是在这杂多的整体中发现自己；在爱里，这个整体并不是作为许多个别的、分离开的东西的总和而被包含着的；在爱里，生命本身发现自己，作为自己的一次加倍，以及这生命的一致；生命从尚未展开的一致出发，通过教养走完了那个通向完成了的一致的圆周；与尚未展开的一致相对而立的，是分离的可能性和世界；在发展中，反思生产出越来越多的对立者，这些对立者在得到满足的冲动中被结合起来，直到它把人自己的整体也摆到他面前与之对立，直到爱在完全的无对象性中扬弃反思，夺走对立者身上一切外来者的性质，而生命无需再有欠缺地找到自己。
在爱里，被分离者还在，但不再是作为被分离者，〔而是〕作为一体的东西，而活的东西感受到活的东西。

en: Because love is a feeling of the living, lovers can be distinguished only insofar as they are mortal, insofar as they think this possibility of separation, not insofar as something would really be separated, insofar as the possible, combined with a being, would be something actual.
In lovers there is no matter, they are a living whole; lovers have independence, their own life-principle — [that] means only: they can die.
The plant has salt and earthy parts that carry in themselves their own laws of their mode of operation — [that] is the reflection of something foreign and means only: the plant can decay.
But love also strives to sublate this distinction, this possibility, as mere possibility, and to unite even the mortal, to make it immortal.

The separable, so long as before the complete union it is still something of its own, causes the lover embarrassment, it is a kind of conflict between the complete surrender, the only possible annihilation, the annihilation of the opposed in the union, and the independence still present; the former feels itself hindered by the latter — love is indignant at what is still separated, at a property; this wrath of love at individuality is shame; it is not a twitching of the mortal, not an expression of the freedom to preserve oneself, to persist; in an attack without love a loving mind is itself offended by this hostility, its shame becomes wrath, which now defends only the property, the right.

If shame were not an effect of love, which only over the fact that something hostile is there has the form of indignation, but were by its nature itself something hostile that wanted to assert an attackable property, then one would have to say of tyrants that they have the most shame, as also of girls who do not give away their charms without money, or of the vain who want to captivate by them.
Both do not love, their defence of the mortal is the opposite of indignation at it; they ascribe to it a value in themselves, they are shameless.
A pure mind is not ashamed of love, but it is ashamed that this is not perfect, it reproaches itself that there is still a power, something hostile, that puts obstacles in the way of completion.

Shame enters only through the memory of the body, through personal presence, at the feeling of individuality — it is not a fear for the mortal, one's own, but before the same, which, as soon as love diminishes the separable, disappears with it; for love is stronger than fear; it does not fear its fear, but accompanied by it, it sublates separations, with the anxiety of finding a resisting, even a firm opposition; it is a mutual taking and giving; shy lest its gifts be scorned, shy lest an opposed thing not yield to its taking, it tries whether hope has not deceived it, whether it wholly finds itself; that which takes does not become richer thereby than the other; it indeed enriches, but the other by just as much; likewise that which gives does not make itself poorer; in giving to the other it has increased its own treasures by just as much; Julia in Romeo: the more I give, the more I have, etc. This wealth of life love acquires in the exchange of all thoughts, all manifoldnesses of the soul, in that it seeks infinite distinctions and finds out for itself infinite unions, turns to the whole manifoldness of nature in order to drink love out of each of its lives.

The most one's own unites itself in contact, in touching, to the point of unconsciousness, the sublation of all distinction; the mortal has laid aside the character of separability, and a germ of immortality, a germ of what eternally develops and begets itself out of itself, a living thing has come to be.
The united does not separate again; the Godhead has worked, created.

But this united thing is only a point, the germ73), the lovers can impart nothing to it that a manifold should be found in it; for in the union no opposed thing has been dealt with, it is pure of all separation; everything through which it can be a manifold, have a determinate being, the newly begotten thing must itself have drawn into itself, opposed and united.
The germ turns away more and more toward opposition and begins; every stage of its development is a separation, in order to win back the whole wealth of life itself.
And so now there is: the one thing, the separated ones, and the reunited.
The united separate again, but in the child the union itself has become undivided.
zh: 因为爱是活的东西的一种感受，所以相爱的人只有在他们是要死的这一点上、在他们想到这种分离的可能性这一点上，才能有区别，而不是在真有什么东西被分离了这一点上，不是在可能的东西与一种存在结合起来就成了现实之物这一点上。
在相爱的人身上没有质料，他们是一个活生生的整体；相爱的人有独立性、有自己的生命原则——〔这〕只意味着：他们会死。
植物有盐分和泥土的成分，它们自身带着自己作用方式的固有规律——〔这〕是一个外来者的反思，只意味着：植物会腐烂。
但爱也力求把这种区别、这种可能性作为单纯的可能性来扬弃，并且把会死的东西本身也结合起来，使它不死。

可分开的东西，只要它在完全的结合之前还是自己的东西，就使相爱的人为难，这是一种冲突，在完全的献身——唯一可能的消灭，即对立者在结合中被消灭——与那还现存的独立性之间；前者觉得自己被后者挡住了——爱对那还被分离的东西、对一份所有物感到不快；爱对个体性的这种恼怒就是羞耻；它不是会死的东西的一下抽搐，不是保存自己、维持自己的那种自由的一次表露；在一种没有爱的攻击面前，一个有爱的心灵被这种敌意本身所冒犯，它的羞耻就变成愤怒，而这愤怒现在只捍卫所有物、捍卫权利。
如果羞耻不是爱的一种作用——爱只是因为有了某种敌意的东西，才取不快这种形态——而是按其本性本身就是某种敌意的东西，想要维护一份可被攻击的所有物，那么人们就得说，暴君是最有羞耻的，同样也得对那些没有钱就不肯交出自己魅力的姑娘说这话，或者对那些想靠魅力把人拴住的虚荣女子说这话。
两者都不爱，他们为会死的东西所作的辩护，与对会死的东西的不快正好相反；他们在自己心里给它安上了一种价值，他们是无耻的。
一颗纯洁的心灵不为爱感到羞耻，但它为爱不完美感到羞耻，它为此责备自己：还有一种力量、一种敌意的东西在，给完成设置障碍。

羞耻只是通过对身体的回忆、通过亲身的在场，在对个体性的感受中才出现的——它不是为会死的东西、为自己的东西而怕，而是在它面前的怕，而这种怕随着爱减少可分开的东西，也同它一起消失；因为爱比怕更强；爱不怕自己的怕，但有怕陪着，它扬弃种种分离，同时怀着担心：会碰到一种抵抗的、甚至牢固的对立；爱是相互的取和给；它怯生生地，怕自己的礼物被鄙弃，怯生生地，怕自己的取遇到一个不肯让开的东西，于是它试一试，希望有没有骗它，它是不是完全找到了自己；取的那一方并不因此比另一方更富；它固然富了，但另一方也同样富了这么多；给的那一方也一样，并不使自己更穷；它给另一方东西时，也就使自己的财富增加了同样多；《罗密欧与朱丽叶》里的朱丽叶说：我给得越多，我就越有，等等。生命的这份财富，是爱在交换一切思想、交换灵魂的一切杂多时挣得的，它寻找无限的差别，为自己找出无限的结合，转向自然的整个杂多，为的是从它的每一个生命里饮到爱。
最切己的东西在接触中、在抚摸中结合起来，直到失去意识、直到一切区别被扬弃；会死的东西放下了可分离性这一性质，于是一颗不死的胚芽、一颗永远从自身中发展并生育自身的胚芽、一个活的东西产生了。
被结合起来的东西不会重新分开；神性起了作用，进行了创造。
但这个被结合起来的东西只是一个点，是胚芽73)，相爱的人不能分给它什么，使其中会有一个杂多；因为在结合中并没有处理过一个对立者，它是纯然没有任何分离的；一切能使它成为一个杂多、能使它有一个定在的东西，都必须由这新生出来的东西自己吸进自身、加以对立并加以结合。
胚芽越来越转向对立、脱离出来，并开始了；它发展的每一个阶段都是一次分离，为的是重新赢回生命自身的全部财富。
于是现在就有了：一体的东西、被分离者、重新结合起来的东西。
被结合起来的人又分开了，但在孩子身上，结合本身成了没有被分开的。

en: This union of love is indeed complete, but it can be so only insofar as the separated is opposed only in such a way that the one is the loving and the other the beloved, that therefore each separated thing is an organ of something living; besides that, however, the lovers still stand in connection with much that is dead, many things belong to each, i.e. it stands in relation to opposed things that are still opposed things, objects, even for the relating one itself; and so they are still capable of a manifold opposition in the manifold acquisition and possession of property and rights.74) The dead thing that is under the power of the one is opposed to both, and it seems that the union over it can only take place in such a way that it would come under the rule of both.

The loving one, which beholds the other in the possession of a property, must feel this particularity of the other, which it has willed; it cannot itself sublate the exclusive rule of the other, for this would again be an opposition against the power of the other, since it can find no other relation to the object than the ruling over it; it would set a ruling against the rule of the other and would sublate a relation of the other, his exclusion of all; and if possession and property make up so important a part of the human being, of his cares and thoughts, then lovers too cannot refrain from reflecting on this side of their relations; and even if the use is common, the right to possession would thereby remain undecided, the thought of right would indeed not be forgotten, because everything in whose possession human beings are has the form of right of property; but if the possessing one also places the other in the same right of possession, then the community of goods is still only the right of each of the two to the thing.
zh: 爱的这种结合虽然是完整的，但它只能完整到这种程度：被分离者只是这样对立着，即一方是爱者，另一方是被爱者，也就是说，每一个被分离者都是一个活的东西的器官；但除此之外，相爱的人还同许多死的东西处在联系中，许多东西属于每个人，也就是说，它同种种对立者处在关系中，而这些对立者对于建立关系的一方自己来说也还是对立者、是客体；于是他们还能够在财产和权利的杂多获取和占有中进行杂多的对立。74) 处在某一方暴力之下的死东西，对双方都是对立的，看来只能这样达成关于它的结合：它落到双方的统治之下。

爱者若看到对方占有某份财产，就必定感受到对方这种它曾意愿过的特殊性；它自己不能扬弃对方的排他统治，因为这会又是对对方权力的一种对立，因为除开对客体的统治，它也找不到对客体的别的关联；它会把一种统治与对方的统治对立起来，并扬弃对方的一种关联，即他对一切人的排除；而如果占有和财产构成人的如此重要的一部分，构成他的忧虑和思想的一部分，那么相爱的人也不能不反思他们关系的这一面；即使使用是共同的，占有上的权利也会因此悬而不决，权利的思想虽然不会被忘记，因为人占有着的一切东西都具有财产的权利形式；但即使占有者把对方也置于同样的占有权利中，财产共有仍然只是双方每一方对物的权利。

en: 75) Faith is the way in which the united, whereby an antinomy is united, is present in our representation.
The union is the activity; this activity, reflected as object, is what is believed.

In order to unite, the members of the antinomy must be felt or cognized as conflicting, and their relation to one another as antinomy; but the conflicting can be cognized as conflicting only by the fact that a union has already taken place; the union is the standard by which the comparison happens, by which the opposed, as such, appear as unsatisfied.

If, now, it is shown that the opposed limited things as such could not subsist, that they would have to sublate themselves, that they therefore, in order to be possible, presuppose a union (already in order to be able to show that they are opposed, the union is presupposed), then it is thereby proved that they must be united, that the union ought to be.

But that the union itself is, is not proved thereby; rather this kind of presence of the representation of it is believed; and [it] cannot be proved, for the opposed are the dependent ones, the union in regard to them [is] the independent one; and to prove means [to show] the dependence; the independent in regard to these opposed can of course again be a dependent, opposed thing in another regard; and then one must again advance to a new union, which is now again what is believed.
zh: 75) 信仰就是那个使一个二律背反得到结合的结合物在我们的表象中现成存在的方式。
结合就是活动；这种活动被反思为客体，就是被信仰的东西。
要结合，二律背反的各项就必须被感受或认识到是互相冲突的，它们彼此的关系必须被感受或认识到是二律背反；但冲突者只有通过已经发生了结合，才能被认识到是冲突者；结合是比较赖以进行的尺度，对立者作为对立者、作为不被满足者，就在这尺度上显现出来。
如果现在表明：那些对立着的有限者作为这样的东西不能持存，它们必定会扬弃自己，因此它们为了可能就必须预设一种结合（单是为了能表明它们是对立者，结合就已经被预设了），那么这就证明了它们必须被结合起来，证明了结合应当存在。
但结合本身存在，并没有由此得到证明，被信仰的倒是关于它的表象的这种现成存在方式；而〔它〕是不能被证明的，因为对立者是依赖者，就对立者而言的结合〔是〕独立者；而证明就意味着〔指出〕依赖；就这些对立者而言的独立者，当然在另一种考虑下又可以是一个依赖者、对立者；于是又必须前进到新的结合，而这新的结合现在又成了被信仰的东西。

en: Union and being are synonymous; in every proposition the copula "is" expresses the union of subject and predicate — a being; being can only be believed; faith presupposes a being; it is therefore contradictory to say that, in order to be able to believe, one must first convince oneself of the being.

It is this independence, the absoluteness of being, that one takes offence at; it is indeed supposed to be, but by the fact that it is, it is for that reason supposed not to be for us; the independence of being is supposed to consist in this, that it is, whether now for us or not for us, being is supposed to be able to be something absolutely separated from us, in which it does not necessarily lie that we come into relation with it; how can something be of which it would yet be possible that we did not believe it? i.e. something is possible, thinkable, which we nevertheless do not believe, i.e. which for that reason is nevertheless not necessary — from thinkability being does not follow; it is indeed in that respect as something thought; but something thought is a separated thing, opposed to the thinker; it is not a being.

Only through this can a misunderstanding arise, that there are different kinds of unions, of being, and that one can therefore say in this respect: something is, but it is not necessary for that reason that I believe it, — with one kind of being another kind of being does not for that reason accrue to it; further, faith is not being, but a reflected being; also in this respect one can say that what is, for that reason still need not [be] reflected, need not come to consciousness.
What is, need not be believed, but what is believed must be.
The thought, now, as something separated must become something united, and only then can it be believed; the thought is a union and is believed; but what is thought, not yet.
zh: 结合和存在是同一个意思；在每一个命题里，系词“是”都表达主词和谓词的结合——一种存在；存在只能被信仰；信仰预设一种存在；所以说，为了能够信仰，人必须先对存在确信，这是自相矛盾的。

让人碰壁的正是这种独立性、存在的绝对性；它固然应当存在，但正因为它存在，它就因此不为我们而存在；存在的独立性据说就在于：它存在，不论为我们还是不为我，存在应当能够是某种绝对与我们分离的东西，其中并不必然包含我们与它发生关系；可是，某种我们完全可能不信仰的东西，怎么能够存在呢？也就是说，有某种可能的东西、可思考的东西，我们却并不信仰它，也就是说，它因此并不必然——从可思考性推不出存在；它在这种意义上固然是作为被思考的东西而有的；但被思考的东西是一个分离者，与思考者相对立；它不是一个存在者。
只有由此才会产生一种误解，以为有不同种类的结合、不同种类的存在，以为人们因此可以这样说：某物存在，但我并不因此就必然信仰它，——有了一种存在，并不因此就有另一种存在归于它；再者，信仰不是存在，而是一种被反思的存在；在这方面也可以说，存在者的东西并不因此就必须被反思、必须进入意识。
存在的东西不必被信仰，但被信仰的东西必定存在。
被思考的东西作为分离者，必须成为被结合起来的东西，然后它才能被信仰；思想是一种结合，并且被信仰；但被思考的东西还不是。

en: The separated finds its union only in one being; for a different being in one respect would presuppose a nature that would also not be nature, thus a contradiction; a union could in the same respect also not be union; a positive faith, now, is one that, instead of the only possible union, sets up another, that puts another being in the place of the only possible being; that therefore unites the opposed in a way through which they are indeed united, but incompletely, i.e. are not united in the respect in which they ought to be united.
zh: 被分离者只在一种存在中找到自己的结合；因为同一种考虑下的另一种存在会预设一种也并非自然的自然，也就是预设一个矛盾；一种结合在同一种考虑下也不可能成为结合；实证信仰则是这样一种信仰：它不用那唯一可能的结合，而立起另一种结合，它把那唯一可能的存在换成了另一种存在；也就是说，它以一种方式结合对立者，这种方式下它们虽然被结合了，但只是不完整地被结合，就是说，它们并没有在它们应当被结合的那种考虑下被结合。

en: All union is supposed to be something given in positive religion; what is given, one does not yet have before one receives it; and after receiving, something given is supposed to be able to remain in part; but something given is in that respect nothing other than an opposed thing, and accordingly the union would be something opposed, namely insofar as it is united, which is a contradiction.

This contradiction arises from an illusion, in that more incomplete kinds of unions, which in another respect are still opposed, are [taken] as an imperfect being for the being that is complete in the respect in which they are to be united, and one kind of being is confused with another kind.
The different kinds of being are the more complete or more incomplete unions.

In every union there is a determining and a being-determined, which are one; in positive religion, however, the determining, even insofar as it determines, is supposed to be determined; its action is not supposed to be an activity, but a suffering; but the determining whereby it suffers is also something united, in this union the acting one could have been active; but this is a lower kind of union; for in the action that happens out of positive faith, this united thing is itself again an opposed thing that determines its opposed, and here there is only incomplete union, for both remain opposed, the one is the determining and the other the determined; and the determining itself is as active, but the form of the activity is determined by another; i.e. [it is supposed to be] given, the active, insofar as it is active, is supposed to be a determined thing; the determining that determines the activity must, as a being, have been united beforehand; if in this union too the determining is supposed to have been a determined thing, then it was determined by another, etc., the positively believing one would have to be an absolutely passive, an absolutely determined thing, which is contradictory. — All positive religions therefore set a more or less narrow limit, into which they restrict activity, they admit certain unions, e.g. intuition, they concede to the human being a certain being, e.g. that he is a seeing, hearing [being], a moving, active one, but of an empty activity; in every determinate activity it is not the active that has determined, but as an active in this respect it is a determinately active one.
zh: 在实证宗教里，一切结合都应当是某种被给予的东西；被给予的东西，人在接受它之前还没有它；而接受之后，被给予的东西应当有一部分还能留下来；但被给予的东西在这种意义上无非是一个对立者，于是结合就会是某种对立的东西，而且是就它被结合起来而言，这就是一个矛盾。
这个矛盾产生于一种迷惑：一些更不完整的结合方式，在另一种考虑下还是对立的，却被〔当成〕不完善的存在，用来顶替在它们应当被结合的那种考虑下完善的存在，于是一种存在被同另一种存在混为一谈。
存在的不同种类，就是较完整或较不完整的结合。

在每一种结合里，都有一个规定和一个被规定，二者是一；但在实证宗教里，规定者即使就它作出规定而言，也应当是被规定的；它的行动不应当是活动，而应当是受动；可是规定者借以受动的那个东西，也是一个被结合起来的东西，在这种结合里，行动者本来可以是活动的；但这是一种较低的结合方式；因为在出于实证信仰的行动里，这个被结合起来的东西本身又成了一个对立者，它规定着自己的对立者，而这里只有不完整的结合，因为双方都还是对立者，一个是规定者，另一个是被规定者；而规定者本身作为活动者，但活动的形式是由另一个东西规定的；也就是说，〔它〕应当是被给予的，活动者就其活动而言，应当是一个被规定者；那个规定活动的规定者，必须作为一个存在者事先已被结合起来；如果在这种结合里规定者也应当曾经是一个被规定者，那它就是由另一个东西规定的，如此等等，那么实证信徒就必须是一个绝对受动的、绝对被规定的东西，而这是自相矛盾的。——所以一切实证宗教都设下一条或宽或窄的界线，把活动限制在里头，它们容许某些结合，例如直观，它们承认人具有某种存在，例如他是一个看东西的、听东西的存在者，〔一个〕运动着的、活动着的东西，但只是一种空洞的活动；在每一种特定的活动里，作出规定的并不是活动者，而是作为这种意义上的活动者，它是一个特定地活动着的东西。

en: The determining is a power through which the activity receives its direction, its form; even when one believes and acts out of trust — trust is identity of the person, of the will, of the ideal, with difference of contingency.
When I, there where I am not he and he is not I, believe him and act according to him, then I am determined, he is a power against me and I comport myself positively toward him.
zh: 规定者是一种权力，活动通过它获得自己的方向、自己的形式；即使人们是出于信任而信仰和行动——信任就是在偶然性不同时人格、意志、理想的同一。
当我在我不是他、他也不是我的地方信仰他并照他行事时，我就被规定了，他就是一种针对我的权力，而我对他就处于实证的关系中。

en: Positive faith demands faith in something that is not — what is not can only either become or not become at all; that which is determined is in that respect no being, and since it is to be believed, it is nevertheless supposed to be a being.

A power is felt, one is passive toward it, and it is not in this feeling, but in the separation of feeling, in which the suffering thing, which in this way becomes object, is opposed to the one effecting the suffering (which in that respect becomes subject).
zh: 实证信仰要求信仰某种不存在的东西——不存在的东西只可能要么生成，要么根本不成；被规定的东西在这种意义上不是存在者，而既然它应当被信仰，它就毕竟应当是存在者。
一种权力被感受到，人对它采取受动的态度，而这种权力并不在这种感受里，而是在感受的分离里，在这种分离中，受动者以这种方式成为客体，与引起受动的那个东西（它在这种意义上成为主体）相对立。

en: All positive religion starts from something opposed, from something that we are not, and that we are supposed to be; it sets up an ideal before its being; in order to be able to believe in it, it must be a power.

In positive religion the being, the union, is only a representation, something thought — I believe that it is, means, I believe in the representation, I believe that I represent something to myself, I believe in something believed (Kant, Godhead); kant.
Philosophy — positive religion.
(Godhead holy will, human being absolute negation; in the representation [it] is united, representations are united — representation is a thought, but what is thought is no being —)
zh: 一切实证宗教都从某种对立的东西出发，从某种我们不是、而我们应当是的东西出发；它把理想立在它的存在之先；为了能够信仰它，它必须是一种权力。
在实证宗教里，存在者、结合只是表象，只是被思考的东西——我相信它存在，意思就是，我相信这个表象，我相信我在向自己表象某种东西，我相信某种被信仰的东西（康德，神性）；kant.
哲学——实证宗教。
（神性即神圣意志，人即绝对的否定；在表象中〔它〕被结合起来，诸表象被结合起来——表象是一种思想，但被思考的东西不是一个存在者——）

en: The letters, of which this translation provides an excerpt, were written by the advocate Cart of Lausanne, who has since died in Philadelphia77); when they appeared in print [1792] they were at once banned by the government in Bern under a heavy fine; for in general they contain an account, grounded on documents, of the political rights of the Pays de Vaud, — a comparison of the condition of the Pays de Vaud, as according to its old rights it ought to have been, with that into which it was brought by the rule of the Bernese; — in particular a history of the ephemeral victory of this government in the year 1791 over the need, revived in the lands of the Vaud, to see their constitution restored, — a victory that was a defeat of their remaining rights and added to the wish for freedom also the deepest bitterness of all minds against their oppressors.

Since this account is given in the form of letters, it at the same time contains the feeling that springs from those events and circumstances; and however much some may thereby easily become distrustful of the credibility of the matter itself — those who demand only pure historical data in order to be all the freer in their judgments and feelings —, this effect is on the one hand less to be feared here, since the rights are proved from documents and the public statute book, and the facts took place before the public; on the other hand, an expression of feeling is necessary for a great many people for the very reason that only through it do they become attentive to the importance of the matter itself, which they would not have felt from the dry statement of the narrative of what happened and of the circumstances, either because they were never in a similar situation, or because they generally live in an unconcerned carelessness and do not suppose that one can lose patience over certain things, and, even if they know the condition of the matter very well, still wonder greatly at the results.
zh: 本译文从中摘出一部分的这些信，作者是洛桑的律师卡尔，他后来已在费城去世77)；这些信 [1792] 印行时，立刻被伯尔尼政府以重额罚金加以禁止；因为它们大体上包含一份以文书为根据的、关于沃州政治权利的陈述，——一种比较：沃州按其旧日权利本该处于什么状态，与它因伯尔尼人的统治而陷入的状态相比；——尤其是一部关于这个政府在 1791 年取得的那场短暂胜利的历史，它战胜的是沃州各地重新苏醒的要求，即要求看到自己的宪法得到恢复，——这场胜利是它剩下的那些权利的一次失败，并且在追求自由的愿望之外，又添上了所有人心里对他们的压迫者最深的愤恨。

由于这份陈述是以书信形式给出的，它同时也就含有从那些事件和情况中产生的情感；而尽管有些人会因此轻易对事情本身的可信性起疑——他们只要求纯粹的历史材料，好在自己的判断和感受上更自由——，这种作用在这里一方面不太可虑，因为那些权利是从文书和公开的法典里得到证明的，事实又是在公众眼前发生的；另一方面，对一大群人来说，把情感表达出来之所以必要，是因为只有这样他们才会注意到事情本身的重要性，而单靠干巴巴地列举发生了什么事和当时的情况，他们是感觉不到这重要性的，原因要么是他们从未处在类似的处境中，要么是他们本来就活得无忧无虑、漫不经心，不认为人在某些事情上会失去耐心，而且即使他们对事情的状况知道得很清楚，还是会对结果大为惊讶。

en: From the comparison of the content of these letters with the most recent events in the Pays de Vaud78), from the contrast between the semblance of the calm enforced in the year 1792, the government's pride in its victory, and the real weakness of that government in this land, its sudden falling away from it, a great many applications would follow; yet the events speak loudly enough for themselves; the only thing that can matter is to get to know them in their entire fullness; they cry out loudly over the earth:
zh: 把这几封信的内容同沃州78)最近的事变加以比较，把 1792 年强行造成的平静的外表、政府对自己胜利的骄傲，同这个政府在这块土地上实际的虚弱、同这块土地对它的突然背离相对照，本可以引出许多教训；不过事变本身已经说得够响了；要紧的只是把它们完完整整地认识清楚；它们向整个大地大声呼喊：

en: Discite iustitiam moniti,
zh: Discite iustitiam moniti，（受告诫者，要学习正义，）

en: but the deaf their fate will seize hard.
zh: 但对听不见的人，命运会重重地抓住他们。

en: The notes are new and contain some data, in part still not known, for the knowledge of the statistics and constitution of Bern.
zh: 这些注释是新加的，其中包含一些——部分是至今还不为人知的——材料，可供了解伯尔尼的统计和宪法。

en: [Cart S. 71: “It is a very great error to measure the goodness of a constitution by the more or fewer levies that one pays under it.
In that case the constitution of England would be the worst of all; for nowhere does one pay so many taxes.

And yet there is no people in Europe that enjoys a greater apparent prosperity and so much individual and national respect. — Because the Englishman is free, because he enjoys the rights that lie in freedom, in a word, because he taxes himself.”]
zh: [Cart S. 71：“按在一部宪法下缴纳的赋税是多是少来衡量这部宪法好不好，是极大的错误。
若如此，英国的宪法就会是所有宪法里最坏的一部；因为没有哪个地方的人缴这么多捐税。
然而欧洲没有一个民族享有比这更大的表面富足，享有这么多来自个人和国家的敬重。——因为英国人自由，因为他享有自由所含的那些权利，一句话，因为他自己向自己征税。”]

en: The author did not live to see how much in the years just past, through the power conceded to the collectors of several taxes, the security of property has in many respects been exposed and the rights of the house diminished, how partly through the suspension of the fundamental law personal freedom, partly through positive laws civil rights have been restricted, — how striking it has become that a minister, through a majority in Parliament that he has made his own, is able to defy public opinion, that the nation is so incompletely represented that it cannot make its voice count in Parliament, and that its security rests more on the fear of its non-constitutional power, on the prudence of the ministers, or on the discretion of the higher estates.
Through this insight and through those facts, respect for the English nation has also sunk even among many of its strongest admirers.

The present inadmissibility of this example has, incidentally, nothing to do with the main proposition that the goodness of the constitution of a country is not to be estimated by the size of the tax that one pays in it.
zh: 作者已经没能活到看见：在刚刚过去的这些年里，由于若干种捐税的征收者获得让与的权力，财产的安全在许多方面被暴露出来、家宅的权利被削减；由于基本法被中止，人身自由受限制，又由于明文法律，市民的权利受限制；——也没能活到看见这变得多么触目：一位大臣凭他在议会里弄到手的多数就能对抗民意，国民被代表得如此不完整，以致它在议会里无法让自己的声音得到重视，而它的安全更多是建立在对自己那种不合宪制的力量的畏惧上，建立在大臣们的精明上，或者建立在上等等级的谨慎上。
由于这种见识，也由于那些事实，对英国国民的敬重，甚至在它的许多最强烈的崇拜者那里也下降了。
这个例子如今不再适用，这跟那条主要命题——衡量一个国家宪法好不好，不能按在其中缴纳的税额大小来定——无关。

en: That, when there was talk of the bad state-form of the canton of Bern, one usually got the answer that the subjects, however, pay almost no taxes, and on that account praised them as happy and enviable, proves only how much less, still very generally, it was held to be to enjoy no civil laws at all than to keep a few talers less in one's pocket yearly.
zh: 人们在谈到伯尔尼州糟糕的国家形式时，通常得到的回答是：臣民几乎不缴什么税嘛，并因此把他们称赞为幸福而令人羡慕，这只能证明一点：绝不享有任何市民法律，在还很普遍的看法里，比每年口袋里少留几个塔勒，被看得轻得多。

en: The tax that the English Parliament laid on the tea to be imported into America was extremely small; but the Americans' feeling that with the altogether insignificant sum which the tax would have cost them the most important right would at the same time have been lost made the American Revolution.
zh: 英国议会对输入美洲的茶叶所征的税极其微小；但美国人有一种感受：随着这笔税本来会让他们付出的、本身完全微不足道的钱，最重要的权利也会一同失去，正是这种感受造成了美国革命。

en: [Cart S. 91: “I do not believe that a greater ethical life prevailed in the Pays de Vaud than in the German part of the canton; but in the Schallwerk one will find ten Germans to one Vaudois.
Should this perhaps come from the fact that in the one land the bailiffs exercise the criminal jurisdiction and in the other they do not?”]
zh: [Cart S. 91：“我不相信沃州的伦理比州里的德语区更好；不过在 Schallwerk 里，人们会发现十个德意志人对一个沃州人。
这难道是因为，在一个地方是总督们行使刑事审判权，而在另一个地方却不是？”]

en: In this respect the Pays de Vaud has many privileges over the German part of the canton; the criminal courts of the Pays de Vaud conduct the proceedings and pronounce in the first instance; the Small Council in Bern has the ius aggratiandi and aggravandi; only in Lausanne does it have the right of pardon alone; in the German canton, by contrast (a few towns excepted), the criminal justice is entirely in the hands of the government, which examines the person accused of a criminal offense and the witnesses and conducts the whole investigation; no counsel is given to the defendant; the record of the investigation is sent to the Small Council, which, according to it and according to a report on it made by the criminal commission, consisting of the three youngest councilors, decides on life and death in the first and last instance; there is no power above it that would have the right of pardon.

In the city the Grossweibel (Grand Sautier, a member of the Great Council, police and civil judge up to a certain competence, and at the same time attendant of the Great and Small Council) conducts the criminal investigation; he deposited this in the chancery for the inspection of the members of the Great Council, the Small Council pronounces in the first instance, the Great Council increases or reduces or confirms this first sentence, whereby the Grossweibel, who had conducted the criminal investigation, appears as official defender.

How little is provided for the delinquent by this defense is easy to understand; hence in his interrogation he will probably try to conceal as much as possible, and thereby will often also conceal some circumstance that mitigates his crime.

By this alone the well-known story becomes intelligible, that a girl was condemned to death as a child-murderer and, when she was to be led to the place of execution, then said to the clergyman that she was sorry only for the child that she carried under her heart; on closer investigation she was then in fact found to be still pregnant with the child for whose murder she was to die in a few hours; when asked why she had not said this earlier, she answered that she had not had the heart to contradict the gracious gentlemen who were interrogating her.
zh: 在这方面，沃州比起州里的德语区有许多特权；沃州的刑事法庭自己承办诉讼并作一审判决；伯尔尼的小议会握有 ius aggratiandi und aggravandi；只有在洛桑，赦免权才单归它所有；而在德语区（少数几个城市除外），刑事司法完全掌握在政府手里，由政府审讯被指控犯了刑事罪行的人和证人，并主持整个调查；被告得不到任何辩护人；调查笔录被送到小议会，小议会根据这份笔录，并根据由三位最年轻的议员组成的刑事委员会就此作出的报告，在一审和终审中判决生死；在它之上没有任何权力拥有赦免权。
在城里，刑事调查由大韦贝尔（Grand Sautier，大议会成员，在一定权限内兼任治安法官和民事法官，同时也是大议会和小议会的侍从）进行；他把调查材料存放在文书房，供大议会成员查阅，小议会作一审判决，大议会则加重、减轻或确认这一初审判决，而主持刑事调查的大韦贝尔便作为官方辩护人出场。
这种辩护能为犯人做的事少得可怜，这很容易明白；所以他在受审时大概会尽量隐瞒，因此也常常会隐瞒一些能减轻他罪行的情节。
单凭这一点就能明白那桩众所周知的事：一个姑娘作为杀婴犯被判处死刑，在她就要被带往刑场时，却对教士说，她只是心疼自己怀里怀着的那孩子；经进一步查验，人们发现她现实地还怀着那孩子，而再过几个钟头，她就要因为杀死这孩子而被处死；问她为什么不早说，她回答说，她没有胆子去反驳那些审讯她的仁慈的老爷们。

en: In the year 1794 a peasant, who had from his commune the testimony that he had always conducted himself well, had never given himself over to drunkenness, and was besides known as a man of limited mind, got into a quarrel with a Bernese gentleman over the settling of accounts for a cartload of wine, during which the peasant had drunk more than he was otherwise accustomed to; the peasant believes he has suffered injustice, and in his drunkenness passes from the exchange of words to abuse of the distinguished gentlemen in general and to the wish that the French might one day humble them.

The Bernese man accuses him of these insults before the bailiff; the peasant, who had been told that he would not better his case by pleading drunkenness, conceals this circumstance in the interrogation, though it would surely have excused his talk, and is sent by the Small Council to the Schallenhaus (the house of correction for greater criminals) for six years.
Through the intercession of the village heads and his relatives, the poor fellow, whom this sentence had made ill, was finally released and then sentenced not to go outside his village for a year.
zh: 1794 年，一个农民跟一位伯尔尼先生因为一车酒的结账起了争执——这农民有村社的证明，说他一向品行良好，从不沉溺于酗酒，而且大家都知道他见识有限——，结账时他喝得比平时多；这农民相信自己受了不公，醉酒中从口角发展到辱骂那些有身份的老爷们，还说希望法国人哪天来把他们羞辱一番。
这个伯尔尼人为此向总督控告他；有人告诉这农民，拿醉酒来辩解并不能改善他的处境，于是他在受审时隐瞒了这一情况，而这一情况本来是可以为那些话开脱的，结果他被小议会送进 Schallenhaus（关押较重罪犯的教养所）六年。
经村长们和他的亲戚出面求情，这个被判决弄病了的可怜人最后被放了出来，随后被判一年之内不得走出自己的村子。

en: I do not wish to infer, from these hasty acts that became known by chance through their correction, that there are many that have not become known; let one judge for oneself whether the course of law did not justify such an inference.
zh: 我不想从这些因为得到纠正才偶然被人知道的草率判决，推断还有许多不为人知的；人们自己判断吧，这种诉讼程序是不是有理由让人作出这样的推断。

en: A custom still in use in many country towns until some time ago indicates that the country people were indeed formerly allowed to have a defender in a criminal case.

On the day appointed for the execution, namely, the local heads assembled under the chairmanship of the bailiff on a public square; a prosecutor comes forward, and after him now follows a defender, who, in the ears of the delinquent, to whom the death sentence had already been announced some days before, strains his lungs to justify him; thereupon the bailiff has the death sentence passed in Bern publicly proclaimed, and the malefactor is led to execution.

This custom, which, by having become a mere formality, was quite outrageous, was abolished some years ago, but with it there was also extinguished the last remaining shadow of one of the most valuable rights of the citizens of civilized states.
zh: 不久以前在许多小城里还很流行的一种做法表明，乡下人从前在刑事案件里大概是可以有辩护人的。
在指定行刑的那天，当地各村的首脑在总督的主持下聚集在一个公共广场上；先有一个控告人出场，接着是一个辩护人，他当着犯人的面——犯人几天前就已经被告知了死刑判决——扯着嗓子拼命为他辩护；随后总督让人公开宣读伯尔尼作出的死刑判决，犯人便被带去行刑。
这种习惯因为已经变成纯粹的形式而变得十分可憎，几年前被废除了，但这样一来，也就抹掉了文明国家市民最可珍视的权利之一所剩的最后一点影子。

en: I also do not want to decide how much of what I shall say falls to the account of the penal process79), which is really no process of law at all, or whether it comes entirely from the immorality of the people or, if one will, from the corruption of human nature, that one finds, as Cart says, ten Germans to one Vaudois in the Schallenhaus, — that, according to my conviction, in none of the countries that I know is so much hanged, broken on the wheel, beheaded, burned in proportion to size as in this canton; without having the authentic proofs for such an assertion, it would perhaps be better not to make it; brought before the public here, it should be a summons to make known, for the sake of this public, the list of those executed in the canton in the last 10 years alone, whereby alone that assertion can be overturned.
zh: 我也不想裁定，我将要说的话里，有多少要归到刑事的诉讼程序79)的罪责上——它其实根本算不上诉讼程序——，又有多少完全出在人民的不道德，或者，随人怎么说，出在人性的败坏，说，如卡尔所说，在 Schallenhaus 里找到的是十个德意志人对一个沃州人，——依我的信念，在我所知道的国家里，没有一个按疆域大小的比例，像这个州这样绞死、轮刑处死、斩首、烧死这么多人；没有确凿的凭据就作这样的断言，也许不如不作；把它拿到公众面前来，它应当是一份呼吁：为了这些公众，只把近 10 年来在这个州被处决者的名单公布出来，因为只有这样，那个断言才能被推翻。

en: For some years the government has itself felt these defects and has had proposals made to it as to how they might be remedied, and has also set a prize on a plan of suitable improvements.
zh: 这几年，政府自己也感觉到了这些弊病，也让人向它提建议，看怎么补救，还为一份适用的改良方案设了赏格。

en: [Cart p. 103 on military billeting in the Pays de Vaud (1791/92): "One does not quarter ten, fifteen, twenty soldiers on a father of a family, or drive him out of his house in order to make a military hospital of it, because he has many rooms, but because he is a patriot; and for the opposite reason the aristocrat is free of it."]
zh: [Cart S. 103，论沃州的军队驻扎（1791/92）："人们把十个、十五个、二十个兵驻到一个一家之父家里，或者把他从自己家里赶出去、把房子改成军医院，并不是因为他有许多房间，而是因为他是个爱国者；而贵族凭相反的理由就免于这一套。"]

en: The quartermasters brought with them from Bern lists of the inhabitants of the towns in which the troops were to be placed.

The fathers of families suspect to the government were marked on this list with an M (mauvais) or MM or even MMM; and according to these signs the quartermaster determined the quantity of soldiers to be quartered on the house, who themselves also soon felt this distinction and behaved accordingly.
In this way these suspect citizens saw themselves punished, for the sole reason that they were suspect, even before the beginning of any investigation.
zh: 军需官从伯尔尼带来了部队将要驻扎的那些城市的居民名册。
在这份名册上，凡被政府视为可疑的一家之父，都用一个 M（mauvais）、或者 MM、甚至 MMM 标出来；军需官就照这些记号决定要往这家塞多少兵，而这些兵自己也很快感觉到了这种区别，并照此行事。
这样一来，这些可疑的市民就仅仅因为自己可疑这一个原因，在任何一种调查还没有开始之前，就已经受到了惩罚。

en: [Cart p. 113: in the case of the Vaudois thrown into the prisons, not the slightest appearance of a crime of high treason had been present.]
zh: [Cart S. 113：对那些被扔进监狱的沃州人来说，连最轻微的一点叛国罪行的迹象都不存在。]

en: The actions that are the ground of the condemnation were signs; they could be regarded as signs of joy over the happily won freedom of the French people, or as signs of a wish to be in the enjoyment of it too, as signs of the resolve to get back one's lawful but lost rights, as signs of the intention to attack the lawful power of the government in an unlawful way: it seems the government has decided that the last intention was present.
zh: 那些构成判决根据的行为是一些标志；它们可以被看作对法国人民幸运地争得的自由感到高兴的标志，也可以被看作一种愿望的标志，即自己也来享受这份自由，可以被看作一种决心的标志，即把自己合法的、但已经丧失的权利重新拿回来，也可以被看作一种意图的标志，即以不合法的方式去攻击政府的合法权力：看来，政府已经认定，最后那种意图是有的。
